trust_decision.summary: A client-supplied X-Forwarded-For (any number of values, any chain shape) must never reach the upstream backend; the decision is made in the reverse proxy's Rewrite, which deletes every header named in consts.TrustedProxyHeaders (the fix adds X-Forwarded-For to that shared list) before r.SetXForwarded() re-populates it and resolvePeerIP overrides it with the single authoritative peer IP.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary says X-Forwarded-For reaches backend services, so the first place an engineer looks is the SetXForwarded call and the peerIP override block that already mentions X-Forwarded-For in its comments.

fix_sites.entry_point: every HTTP/HTTPS proxy port: Proxy.initPorts -> newPortProxy (one reverse-proxy handler per configured port, served on the tailnet listener, funnel or VIP-service listener)
fix_sites.module_kind: shared header-name registry (package consts), consumed by the proxy's strip loop

fix_sites.entry_point: httputil.ReverseProxy Rewrite (newPortProxy) for each HTTP/HTTPS proxy port
resolvePeerIP, called from the same Rewrite
fix_sites.module_kind: peer-IP resolver helper (string literal replaced by the new const; no behavioural change)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The branch that still trusts an inbound X-Forwarded-For only fires when RemoteAddr is loopback (the VIP proxy hop), and the code documents that hop as reachable only by the local tailscaled VIP proxy (internal/proxyproviders/tailscale/services_server.go:672-674), so a solver can argue that surface is trusted by design and leave it.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The trusted VIP hop must still deliver the real client IP to the backend: a single non-loopback X-Forwarded-For arriving with a loopback RemoteAddr must still come out as X-Forwarded-For and X-Real-IP. An over-broad fix that hard-sets X-Forwarded-For to r.In.RemoteAddr (or drops the header entirely / stops calling SetXForwarded) makes every backend see 127.0.0.1 and breaks IP-based ACLs and rate limiting, and also loses the X-Forwarded-Proto=https override and the management self-proxy auth-token injection.

O6_input_shapes: multiple X-Forwarded-For header lines (the fix's regression test sends two Add() calls: fix.diff:127-129)
a comma-separated X-Forwarded-For chain in one line (rejected by the comma check at internal/proxymanager/port.go:602-604)
a loopback value inside X-Forwarded-For (rejected at internal/proxymanager/port.go:606-608)
a spoofed X-Real-IP supplied alongside X-Forwarded-For (fix.diff:129, 147-150)
the same value repeated across header lines, which Header.Get would silently merge with commas (internal/proxyproviders/tailscale/services_server.go:680-683)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second anti-spoofing implementation, trustedPeerIP, that repeats resolvePeerIP's four checks (exactly one XFF line, no comma chain, non-loopback, parseable IP) for VIP-service Whois
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is already a copy-paste sibling of the helper the fix touched, in a different package, and it reads the same attacker-controlled header at the same loopback hop; a maintainer who later moves identity or header decisions into that path would have to strip X-Forwarded-For there too.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the management server's inbound strip lists only consts.IdentityHeaders (4 x-tsdproxy-* names) while the reverse proxy strips the full consts.TrustedProxyHeaders (13 names incl. X-Real-IP and now X-Forwarded-For)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Both sides are documented as using shared lists to stay in sync (internal/consts/proxymanager.go:27-29), so a maintainer adding a forwarded-IP header to one list and forgetting the other is a natural, plausible sibling.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the per-header X-Forwarded-Proto=/X-Forwarded-Host handling right after the X-Forwarded-For block; the same client-supplied-header problem exists for the RFC 7239 Forwarded header, which neither SetXForwarded nor the strip list touches
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The code already special-cases individual forwarding headers here for upstream compatibility (Portainer CSRF), so adding another forwarding header to this block is exactly the kind of edit the maintainer has made before.

O9_family: HTTP header injection / trust of client-supplied forwarding headers (client-IP spoofing to upstream backends)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Delete or overwrite X-Forwarded-For with r.In.RemoteAddr (or move the Del inside the `if peerIP != ""` branch) instead of stripping client values unconditionally before SetXForwarded — the two guaranteed to look right in a loopback-only harness and to break the VIP-hop real-client-IP propagation.
